message.content: {"summary":"Your report is well structured and reaches a clearly justified 'Not Ship' recommendation, supported by the EA Code of Ethics and two strong case studies (NHS, VW). Your introduction identifies the core dilemma and stakeholders, and your for/against discussion is balanced. To reach the top band, develop several distinct ethical issues, give decision guidance to all stakeholders, strengthen evidence for weaker arguments, and add visual elements while fixing language errors.","next_steps":["Add a stakeholder-by-stakeholder decision-making discussion (health department, end-users, chip contractor), not just Rachel and her company, to lift C2 to Excellent.","Support the 'ship now to fund future QA' argument in 'The Most Ethical Path' with evidence or a case study, or remove/reframe it, and state an explicit criterion for when shipping with known defects could be acceptable.","Add visual elements (e.g. a stakeholder-interests table, decision matrix or risk-benefit figure), correct 'DICUSSION' and 'EACE' to 'EA', fix grammatical errors, and complete reference [3] with a URL."],"criteria":{"C1":"Your introduction clearly identifies the central dilemma (public safety vs business pressure) and lists stakeholders, including Rachel, her company, the chip contractor and the health department. To reach Excellent, develop several distinct ethical issues with their significance — e.g. professional integrity, reputational risk, and end-user safety as separate issues — rather than one core dilemma.","C2":"Your for/against arguments (competitive advantage and revenue vs harm, integrity and reputation) show reasonable depth and lead to a clear conclusion. The next level requires decision-making recommendations for several different stakeholders — currently your guidance focuses on Rachel and her company, with little for the health department or end-users.","C3":"Your report follows a logical for/against structure that builds well to the 'Not Ship' conclusion, supported by the harm case study, the EA Code and reputation arguments. To reach Excellent, fully resolve the 'grow now to fix QA later' argument in 'The Most Ethical Path' so every strand of the argument supports the conclusion systematically.","C4":"Your four references, including the NHS IT failures and VW emissions case studies with quantitative evidence (lost letters, fines), substantiate key arguments well. For Excellent, ensure every argument is evidenced — the future-QA-improvement claim currently has no support — and replace the tangential Apple marketing source with one directly relevant to competitive advantage.","C5":"Your report has all required sections and IEEE-style references, and reads fluently overall. However, it contains no figures, tables or visual elements, and has language errors: 'DICUSSION', repeated use of 'EACE' instead of EA, 'benefits of could very well', and 'have her company might go under'. Fixing these and adding visuals would lift you to Very good or Excellent."}}
